title: Harmeet Desai, Yashaswini Ghorpade End India's 72-Year Mixed Doubles Wait
excerpt: The Indian pair beat South Korea in a five-game quarter-final in Tashkent and took bronze at the Asian Table Tennis Championships, India's first mixed doubles medal since 1954.
body:
• Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade won bronze in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent, India's first medal in the event in 72 years.
  • The Indian pair beat South Korea's Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun 3-2 in the quarter-final, coming back from 1-2 down to win 11-6, 8-11, 8-11, 11-9, 11-9 in 42 minutes.
  • They lost their semi-final to Japan's Sora Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto in straight games, 9-11, 9-11, 8-11, and returned with the bronze.
  • India's previous mixed doubles medals at the championships were gold in 1952 and silver in 1954.

India ended a 72-year wait for a mixed doubles medal at the Asian Table Tennis Championships on Friday, as Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade secured bronze in Tashkent with a five-game quarter-final win that held up as a podium finish.

The Indian pair defeated South Korea's Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun 3-2 in the quarter-final to reach the semi-finals and assure India of a medal, according to an IANS report published by hi INDiA. It is the first time India has won a mixed doubles medal at the championships since 1954.

A comeback that secured the medal

The Bridge reported that Ghorpade and Desai took the opening game, then fell behind as the South Korean pair won the next two, before recovering to close out the match 11-6, 8-11, 8-11, 11-9, 11-9 in a quarter-final that lasted more than 42 minutes. Winning the fourth and fifth games by the same 11-9 margin turned a match that was slipping away into the result that ended the medal drought.

In the semi-final, the Indians faced Japan's Sora Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto. The Bridge reported that Ghorpade and Desai stayed close in every game but lost in straight games, 9-11, 9-11, 8-11, and returned with the bronze medal.

First podium finish since 1954

The last Indians to win a mixed doubles medal at the Asian Table Tennis Championships were Yatin Vyas and Meena Parande, who won silver in 1954, The Bridge reported. Two years earlier, at the inaugural championships in 1952, Kalyanpur Jayant and Gool Nasikwala won gold. Desai and Ghorpade's bronze is only India's third mixed doubles medal in the history of the event, and the first in more than seven decades.

India's second mixed doubles pair in Tashkent did not reach the medal round. Payas Jain and Syndrela Das lost their quarter-final 0-3 to China's Yi Chen and Huang Youzheng, the IANS report said.

A medal after near misses

The bronze follows a recent run in which both players came home without medals. At the recent Asian Games, Desai competed in three events: India's men's team reached the round of 16 before losing to South Korea, he and Ghorpade reached the mixed doubles quarter-finals before losing to China's Lin Shidong and Kuai Man, and he and Sathiyan Gnanasekaran went out in the third round of the men's doubles to Japan's Matsushima and Shunsuke Togami, according to the IANS report.

Ghorpade also returned from the Asian Games without a medal. She lost in the third round of the women's singles to Japan's Miwa Harimoto, the same player she faced in Friday's semi-final, and she and Diya Chitale reached the women's doubles quarter-finals before losing 0-3 to China's Fan Shuhan and Chen Yi.

Against that background, Friday's quarter-final comeback carries weight beyond a single bronze. A pairing that had stopped at the quarter-final stage against the world's top combinations has now converted that position into a continental medal, and broken a sequence stretching back to before most of Indian table tennis's modern era began.
